text:
The shifting executory interest in the sister’s children who reach 25 was void from the 1960 conveyance under the common-law Rule Against Perpetuities: church use, and an afterborn child’s twenty-fifth birthday, can both occur more than 21 years after every life then in being has died. Striking it leaves the friend with a fee simple absolute; later births and deaths do not revive the gift, and neither an open class for the sister’s life nor a 21-year period after the afterborn son’s death is a valid measuring period. Title is in the friend only.

CONFIDENCE: 88
